findings.evidence: `condExp_condExp_of_le` (mathlib/.../ConditionalExpectation/Basic.lean:344) requires only `m₁ ≤ m₂ ≤ m₀` plus `SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm₂)` — no integrability (it dispatches `hf : Integrable f μ` internally at line 348) — and `IsFiniteMeasure μ` supplies the sigma-finiteness, so the reduction is unconditional. This is exactly the route Mathlib's upward proof takes (line 441-445, via `μ[g | ⨆ n, ℱ n]`).
findings.fix: Drop `h_f_int` from `tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp_iInf` (and, for consistency, from `tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf` / the private lemma) by applying the current integrable-case lemma to `g := μ[f | 𝔽 0]`, which is integrable by `integrable_condExp`, and rewriting with `condExp_condExp_of_le (h_filtration (Nat.zero_le n)) h_le0` and `condExp_condExp_of_le (iInf_le 𝔽 0) h_le0` to recover `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` and `μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n]`.
findings.issue: `h_f_int : Integrable f μ` is stronger than the Mathlib convention this PR claims to mirror: `MeasureTheory.tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp (g : Ω → ℝ)` (mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Martingale/Convergence.lean:439) and `tendsto_ae_condExp` (ibid. :426) take no integrability hypothesis, since `condExp` is `0` for non-integrable arguments and the statement is then trivially true.

summary: The new L¹ theorem carries an integrability hypothesis that Mathlib's upward analogue deliberately omits and that is removable by the same tower trick Mathlib uses; the statements are otherwise at the right level.
